title: Designing the SICR assessment under IFRS 9
dek: Relative and absolute PD thresholds, qualitative triggers and the evidence needed to support a Stage 2 population
summary: How a relative PD threshold behaves across a rating scale, which triggers stage the demo portfolio, and how much the allowance moves when the threshold changes.

title: Lifetime PD under IFRS 9: from transition matrix to forward-looking curves
dek: Compounding a rating transition matrix, summarising macroeconomic scenarios in a credit cycle index, and probability-weighting the result
summary: Deriving lifetime PD curves from one transition matrix, adjusting them for macroeconomic scenarios, and why the weighted allowance in the demo portfolio is 23.8% above the baseline.

title: Credit stress testing and capital: migration, risk-weighted assets and reverse stress
dek: Taking a loan-level credit stress through to the CET1 ratio, explaining the movement, and quantifying the distance to the hurdle
summary: Taking a credit stress through rating migration, risk-weighted assets and earnings to the CET1 ratio, with a quantified reverse stress test on the demo bank.

title: Non-maturity deposits in IRRBB: core balances, slotting and their effect on ΔEVE
dek: How the core deposit assumption is built under the Basel standardised framework, and how far it moves the economic value and earnings measures
summary: How the core deposit split is built under the Basel standardised framework, and how the same balance sheet moves from an EVE outlier to an NII outlier as the core assumption changes.

title: Measuring IRRBB under the standardised framework: shocks, outlier tests and where the risk sits
dek: Slotting repricing cash flows, constructing the six supervisory shocks, and reading ΔEVE, ΔNII and key-rate sensitivities together
summary: Building the six supervisory shocks, the EVE and NII outlier tests, and key-rate PV01s on the demo bank, and why its economic value and earnings move in opposite directions.

title: Building a bank model that will stand up to review
dek: The structure, formula conventions and integrity checks that internal validation, auditors and supervisors look for, with examples from three models
summary: The structure, formula conventions and integrity checks that make a spreadsheet model reviewable, with examples from the IFRS 9, stress testing and IRRBB models.

title: Reviewing a model you did not build: what integrity checks catch and what they miss
dek: Four common errors planted in a copy of a working IRRBB model, the checks that found two of them, and the tests that find the other two
summary: Four errors planted in a copy of a working model: the integrity checks caught two, and the other two needed a scenario test to find. A review procedure for inherited and AI-built models.

title: Which assumptions move the answer: ranking sensitivities in an IFRS 9 model
dek: A loan-level model has hundreds of inputs. Flexing them one at a time shows that a few judgements carry most of the result.
summary: Flexing six assumptions in a 1,000-loan IFRS 9 model one at a time: two judgements, the scenario weights and the unsecured loss rate, move the allowance more than the other four combined.
